subject: English
summaryPoints: The simple past tense denotes actions completed within a finished time frame accompanied by explicit past time adverbials (yesterday, last month, in 2010, two days ago).
The present perfect tense expresses actions completed at an unspecified indefinite time, recent events with present consequences, or experiences within an unfinished period.
Negative and interrogative past simple sentences require the auxiliary 'did / didn't' combined strictly with the bare infinitive of the lexical verb.
Present perfect utilizes experiential adverbial particles such as 'already', 'yet', 'ever', 'never', 'just', and 'so far'; 'yet' appears solely in negative statements and questions.

Unit phrasal verbs include 'count on' (depend/rely upon), 'count up' (calculate total), 'crack down on' (enforce disciplinary measures), 'cross off' (delete from list), 'cut back' (reduce output), and 'cut down' (reduce consumption).
Social studies themes differentiate 'equality' (providing everyone with identical inputs) from 'equity' (tailoring inputs to individual needs to attain fairness).

formulas.label: Simple Past Structure (Completed Time)
formulas.expr: Affirmative: S + V2  |  Negative: S + did not + V1(base)  |  Interrogative: Did + S + V1(base) + ... + past time marker (yesterday, ago, last year)

formulas.label: Present Perfect Structure (Indefinite / Experiential)
formulas.expr: Affirmative: S + has/have + V3  |  Negative: S + has/have not + V3 + yet  |  Interrogative: Have/Has + S + ever + V3?

examTip: Whenever an exact past time marker (e.g., 'yesterday', 'ago', 'in 1998', 'last night') appears in an EUEE sentence, you MUST use the simple past tense (V2), NEVER the present perfect tense. Incorrect: 'I have finished my work yesterday.' Correct: 'I finished my work yesterday.'

keyDefinitions.definition: A tense indicating that an action or situation occurred and was concluded in past time, separated from the present moment.
The state of providing identical opportunities, resources, or treatment to all individuals regardless of starting disparities.
The principle of fairness that allocates differentiated, tailored resources and support according to specific needs to eliminate structural disadvantages.
A sworn body of impartial citizens assembled to evaluate evidence in a court of law to deliver a verdict on legal proceedings.

eueeFocusTopics: Past simple with definitive past time markers vs present perfect without them
Phrasal verbs based on 'cut' and 'count' ('cut back', 'cut down on', 'crack down on')
Conceptual distinction between equality, equity, and judicial fairness
